A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPFormer with the same authors and core research design. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and technical appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SemanticKITTI experiments, architectural ablations, qualitative predictions, class-wise results, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds cross-dataset generalization, matching-threshold evaluation, and further training and loss ablations.

M1.justification: The architecture and default training objectives remain substantially unchanged. However, Eq. (5) replaces g(DSA(...)) with DSA(...)+W_I. Because v1 does not define g, the PDFs cannot establish whether the explicit learnable embeddings represent a procedural change or clarification of the existing generator.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only SemanticKITTI. v2 adds zero-shot PSC and SSC evaluation on the distinct SSCBench-KITTI360 test set using SemanticKITTI-trained models, substantially extending coverage to an unseen data distribution.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate MonoScene, Symphonies, OccFormer, and CGFormer with DBSCAN. The added generalization experiment extends CGFormer+DBSCAN to another dataset. Newly discussed PanoOcc and SparseOcc are not evaluated, and PanoSSC remains unavailable for direct comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces cross-dataset zero-shot testing and relative performance-gap reporting. Tables 9–10 add evaluation at a 20% matching threshold and controls varying depth, Dice, focal-loss, and SSC-loss settings. The original SemanticKITTI split, 25/30-epoch training budget, and standard 50% matching setting are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test distribution-shift robustness, sensitivity to the matching threshold, and loss-dependent SSC–PSC tradeoffs. Table 10 combines configurations already present in v1 Table 5 with additional loss and hyperparameter variants and SSC measurements; it substantially extends the original ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its experiments. Both present point estimates; discussion of uncertainty concerns cited PaSCo work.

E6.justification: All original tabulated results match after accounting for relocation. New Table 2 reports KITTI360 PQ-All of 1.23 versus CGFormer+DBSCAN's 1.08, although Thing PQ/RQ are slightly lower. Table 9 adds PQ-All of 12.74 under 20% matching versus 6.30 under 50% matching. Table 10 adds configuration results and SSC scores.

T1.justification: Sec. 3.2 revises the voxelization set S by replacing Q(F3D(u,v,d,c)) with Q((u,v,d,c)), correcting the formal assignment to use coordinates rather than feature values. The added PQ† and focal-loss formulas explain existing choices; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The context-adaptive proposal contribution and runtime claim remain. v2 adds superior zero-shot generalization as a headline claim in the abstract, contributions, and conclusion, and reframes the dual-head/two-stage contribution as balancing metrics rather than improving three of four All-category metrics.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief discussion of SSC–PSC noncorrelation, v2 develops explanations of SSC–PSC and Thing–Stuff tradeoffs under different losses and training configurations (A.3, A.7). It also attributes transfer performance to context adaptivity and explains the recognition–segmentation tradeoff under relaxed matching. Existing rare-class and PanoSSC-comparison limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link, official baseline-checkpoint provenance, PyTorch/fp32 implementation information, focal-loss defaults, and explicit generator and PQ† matching details. These improve documentation; they do not establish changes to the retained hardware, optimizer, grid resolution, or training budget.

R1.justification: Sec. 2 adds PanoOcc and SparseOcc, distinguishing temporal/surround-view approaches from IPFormer's forward-facing, non-temporal setting, and removes CAL. SSCBench and PyTorch references are also added. The broader SSC review and central context-adaptivity positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, rewrites the PSC related-work discussion and experimental framing, expands selected explanations, and reorganizes the appendix. Most methodological prose and the overall section hierarchy remain intact, so the language and structural revision is limited.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 9, and 10 and merges v1's SSC Table 8 into Table 1. Figures 1 and 3 receive panel borders and arrangement refinements; Figure 2 clarifies depth-estimation and SSC connections. Retained tables and qualitative figures are relocated, with the underlying qualitative examples unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added cross-dataset evaluation and targeted threshold/loss analyses provide useful evidence beyond v1's single-dataset study, while implementation disclosures improve transparency. The benefit is limited by overstatements: Table 2 retains Thing PQ/RQ exceptions to the broad superiority claim, and Table 10 contradicts the prose claim of second-best PQ-Stuff. Overall, empirical support improves, but the new interpretations require more precision.
